title: content/home/home.json
description: M7-04 — the loc keys the Home screen (S03) renders. What is fixed here is that the screen shows a Legend Level label, an Energy label, an Energy Reserve label, the HUD tiles' captions (Crowns, Soul Shards, Gold, Power, Progress, Stage, and the three tier names the progress tile spells a clear with), one primary action caption per run decision, one status line per state the screen can be in while it has nothing to act on, and the line a progress tile shows before anything is cleared — and that every one of them is a key rather than a literal (X-04). The currency and tier captions are keys other documents own; they are named here as well so that Home's dependence on them is a reference the loader checks rather than a literal in a presenter. Every value is a loc key, so ContentInvariants.CheckLocaleKeyReferences resolves it against every locale file: a key this document names but a locale does not carry fails the build, and a locale string this document stops naming fails it as an orphan. additionalProperties is false on every object so the absences are enforced rather than merely observed: there is no member for an Energy maximum, a regeneration countdown, a Legend-XP percentage or a run Energy cost. Those are functions of tuning that only Core can evaluate, and a slot here would hold a NUMBER rather than a key — which is the second copy of the formula. ⚠️ The screen does now show three of the four: Core.Rules.Economy.HomeEnergyView projects the maximum, the countdown and the price out of the readers that are internal to Core, and they arrive as values through the host seam rather than as anything authored here. This document still authors no member for them, and that is still right: what it authors is loc keys. home-run-hub Phase 3b added the run hub's own strings: the stage card's two lines and its no-next-chapter stand-in, the hero band's caption, the five tab captions, the three side-rail captions, and one action word per launch state the primary button can be in plus the stage card's Change and the top bar's Settings. additionalProperties stays false, so the absences are still enforced: there is no member for a reward tag, because no reward vocabulary is authored anywhere in game-data/, and none for a tab or rail badge, because a dot is a flag over stored state and carries no words.

locKey.description: loc.<domain>.<id>.<field>, lowercase, dot-separated, snake_case segments — the same shape schema/loc.schema.json governs the locale files by.

label.description: The captions beside the header values the player snapshot carries, and the HUD tiles' captions. Energy and Energy Reserve are two separate banks and are labelled separately: one caption over both would read as a single pool, which is not what the state says. crowns, soulShards and gold name the currency names, and tierNormal, tierHeroic and tierMythic name Chapter Select's tier names: keys those documents own, declared here because the HUD renders them and a dependency the loader cannot see is one a retired key breaks silently.

action.description: The primary button, in the two shapes the run decision can take. Two captions rather than one parameterised caption: 'start a new run' and 'resume the run you are in' send the player to different places, and a screen that says the same word for both is a screen a player cannot read.

status.description: The line shown while the screen has no decision to offer — the read has not answered yet, the read said there is no such profile, the run the player left has lapsed — and the one line a tile shows in place of a value: nothingCleared is what the progress tile says on a profile that has cleared no chapter. The CAUSE beyond that is carried in code as a named state so it can be logged and told apart, while what a player is shown stays one honest sentence — which is exactly why launchFailed exists: the launch block catches an exception, keeps its type and message as the DIAGNOSTIC it logs, and shows this authored line instead, because a raw type name on a phone is a sentence nobody can act on. notOpenYet is the one acknowledgement every destination this build has no screen for gives back on a tap, and refillNotOpenYet is that same acknowledgement worded for the refill offer, where the player is blocked and the honest next step — Energy returning on its own, counted down in the top bar — is already on the screen. Neither may read as an offer to buy Energy: this game has no real-money currency of any kind.
